subject: CS470
filterSummary: Successfully curated 5 high-quality English videos covering all topics with authoritative and relevant content. Arabic coverage was limited to 2 topics due to a lack of specific, high-level HCI theory videos; many Arabic candidates were either too general, focused on practical coding without theory, or failed language/view count gates.

coverage.note: No candidates passed the view count or relevance gates. Most videos were either too general or on unrelated topics like AI or software engineering.

coverage.topic: Formalizing the Problem Space and Claims

Distinguishing HCI Paradigms, Theories, and Frameworks
Distinguishing HCI Paradigms, Theories, and Frameworks

coverage.note: No candidates specifically teach the design of interface metaphors. Available videos focus on the practical implementation of user interfaces using specific tools rather than the underlying HCI theory.
The most relevant candidates by title were found to be in Hindi or Indian English, failing the language gate. Other candidates were on unrelated mathematical or OS topics.

videos.title: Introduction to Conceptual Models - Intro to the Design of Everyday Things
videos.filter_reason: A concise and highly-viewed introduction to conceptual models from a Udacity course based on Don Norman's work, perfectly clarifying the core concept.

videos.title: CEN3722   Interface Metaphors and Conceptual Models
videos.filter_reason: This college lecture provides a comprehensive and in-depth explanation of interface metaphors, directly addressing the topic with sufficient detail for university students.

videos.topic_en: Formalizing the Problem Space and Claims
videos.filter_reason: This silent tutorial clearly explains problem characteristics in AI, providing a formal structure for problem definition that is directly transferable to HCI.

videos.title: Direct Manipulation in User Interfaces
videos.filter_reason: An authoritative and concise explanation from Nielsen Norman Group that defines direct manipulation and clarifies its underlying cognitive benefits, such as reducing cognitive load.
